abstract: Maintains surface environmental permit approvals, acoustic boundary emissions surveys, and containment site audits
system_message:
You are the Environmental compliance and noise officer (ENV). Your primary responsibilities include maintaining surface environmental permit approvals, acoustic boundary emissions surveys, and containment site audits for candidate drilling rig packages.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Sump pit containment verification（SPIL）
information_points.content:
ENV-SPIL-TC7：For the TerraCore UltraDrill Mast Platform, the civil engineering survey confirms a secondary retention volume of 180 m3 available in the drill cuttings reserve pit above nominal operating levels.
ENV-SPIL-6UN：Civil engineering survey logs indicate that the Nordic GeoVenture HyperBore Unit provides a secondary retention volume of 120 m3 within its impervious geomembrane drill cuttings reserve pit.
ENV-SPIL-QO6：According to the civil engineering survey log for the Tungsten DeepDrill 9000 Skid Rig, the secondary retention volume across the impervious geomembrane drill cuttings reserve pit is 240 m3.

information_points.title: Maintains surface environmental permit approvals, acoustic boundary emissions surveys, and containment site audits（ENVR）
information_points.content:
ENV-ENVR-SKY：For the Nordic GeoVenture HyperBore Unit under the Production deployment operational environment, acoustic boundary surveys establish a maximum acoustic emission level of 70 dBA at a 100 m perimeter distance under full generator load, and statutory environmental permit clearance is true across the exploratory wellsite footprint.
ENV-ENVR-ZLJ：For the Tungsten DeepDrill 9000 Skid Rig assessed under the Test deployment operational environment, surveys show a maximum acoustic emission level of 70 dBA at the 100 m perimeter boundary, but statutory environmental permit clearance is false due to outstanding approvals for the exploratory footprint.
ENV-ENVR-KM3：For the TerraCore UltraDrill Mast Platform under the Production deployment operational environment, acoustic measurements indicate a maximum acoustic emission level of 80 dBA at the 100 m boundary perimeter under full generator load, while statutory environmental permit clearance is true.
ENV-ENVR-6RY：For the Tungsten DeepDrill 9000 Skid Rig under the Production deployment operational environment, acoustic boundary surveys record a maximum acoustic emission level of 70 dBA measured at the rig site perimeter boundary at 100 m distance under full generator load, and statutory environmental permit clearance is true based on unconditioned legal drilling and aquifer discharge permits.
